data.long_meaning: Anishka is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Anisha’, which means ‘Goddess of Peace’. This name is associated with calmness, tranquility, and serenity. The name Anishka carries the meaning “Goddess of Peace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anishka usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of peace and live with faith, good character and purpose.

For parents naming their child 'Anishka', it is often chosen to instill a sense of calmness and strength in the child, as they grow and develop.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of Anishka lies in the name's connection to the Hindu Goddess of Peace. As a young Hindu girl grows into womanhood, her name is a constant reminder of the importance of seeking inner peace and maintaining a calm, peaceful demeanor, in the turbulent world around her. Anishka is an emblem of tranquility and a guiding symbol of enduring strength and wisdom for the named person.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Anishka: Radiant and pure like the untouched mind in deep meditation, Anishka embodies inner peace and wisdom. The name signifies the spiritual journey towards enlightenment and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Anishka was the name of a legendary Hindu princess who lived during the Gupta Empire period in India (circa 4th to 6th century CE). She is known for her exceptional beauty and wisdom. According to mythology, she was cursed by a sage to forget her past life, and so she renounced her royal life and became a wandering ascetic.

Anishka is also the name of a celestial being in Hindu astronomy, representing the star beta Canis Majoris (Sirius B). This star was believed to have influence over human emotions and was worshipped as a goddess. Ancient Hindu texts such as the Mahabharata and the Puranas mention Anishka as a star deity.
